slides.subtitle: Agentic Futures, Curricular Sustainability
slides.meta: Wednesday, July 22, 2026 · 10 AM – noon · CHDR · last in-person session

slides.title: A tour, not a tutorial
slides.lead: We look at what is just beyond Code Web — Cowork, the Claude CLI, MCP, the Superpowers workflow — so you leave with a map. The hands-on portion is a *writing* exercise.

slides.title: What is an agent?
bullets: **Tool use:** the model can call functions you give it (search, file edit, run command).
**Planning:** the model decides what to do next, in what order.
**Subagents:** the model can spawn helper instances of itself.
An *agent* is the loop these compose into. The vocabulary is doing a lot of work.

slides.title: Cowork tour
slides.lead: Live walkthrough of a Cowork session — Claude working alongside you in real time on a shared problem. We use one of *your* W7 or W9 artifacts as the working surface.

slides.title: Cowork on your ePortfolio or playful tool
slides.note: What changes when the conversation is collaborative rather than turn-taking. Bring a question that's been nagging at your site.

slides.title: Claude CLI tour
slides.lead: Claude in the terminal. Slash commands, `/init`, `/plan`, `CLAUDE.md` for context engineering, the Superpowers workflow.

slides.title: Claude CLI on a small humanities project
slides.note: Brainstorm → Spec → Plan → Implementation → Review. You watch. You don't install.

slides.title: Superpowers as a discipline
bullets: **Brainstorm:** explore intent before any code.
**Spec:** write the design as a checked-in artifact.
**Plan:** decompose into reviewable steps.
**Implementation:** test-driven, gated by review checkpoints.
**Review:** verification before completion claims.

slides.title: MCP, briefly
slides.lead: Model Context Protocol — 'USB-C for AI.' One example: connecting Claude to a Zotero library so research and writing share a context.

slides.title: Why MCP matters for the next academic year
bullets: Connect Claude to a tool *you already use* (Zotero, Google Drive, your library catalog).
Now your AI workflow shares the same context as your research.
Each MCP integration is a *humanities choice*: which of your tools deserves to be in the loop?

slides.title: Revisiting text — and labor
slides.lead: Before we write a `CLAUDE.md`, the labor question. The Underwood essay you read frames it; this is the practitioner's version.

slides.title: Altman: 'jobs that aren't real work'
bullets: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/sam-altman-says-ai-could-eliminate-jobs-that-arent-real-work): the CEO's framing of which jobs disappear.
Whose work is 'not real'? Look at the verbs.
Most of what humanists do is on his list.

slides.quote: The point of bullshit jobs isn't that the work is hard or the workers are lazy. It's that the work is *meaningless*, and the worker knows it. AI is being marketed as the cure. It is at least as likely to be a more efficient producer.
slides.attribution: Echoing David Graeber's *I Had to Guard an Empty Room*

slides.title: Write your `CLAUDE.md`
slides.lead: A context file an agent could read to understand your work. Whether or not you ever install the CLI, this document is a deliverable in its own right.

slides.title: Your `CLAUDE.md` in 30 minutes
steps: **Who you are and what you do.** One paragraph.
**Your domain.** Disciplines, methods, topics, key conversations.
**Your typical workflows.** What you tend to ask AI for; what you do *not* want it to do.
**Your preferences.** Citation style, voice, audience defaults.
**Your boundaries.** What you will not delegate. What requires your hand.

slides.quote: The most important sentence in any conversation about agentic AI is: *what would I have to give up to use this?* The answer is rarely zero.

slides.title: Closing thoughts from the source class
bullets: We started in May with ELIZA. We end in July with `CLAUDE.md`.
The through-line: refuse to gesture vaguely. Name the labor. Name the choice.
Take what is useful. Stay skeptical of the rest.
